title: High-Ticket Brokerage — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Worksheets for vetting commission seats, choosing your intermediary lane, staying inside broker-dealer and licensing rules, and protecting deals with non-circumvention paper and disciplined yacht and aircraft entry plans

worksheets.title: Commission Seat Vetting and Intermediary Lane Selection
worksheets.purpose: Pressure-test a high-ticket closing seat before you commit your calendar to it, build the call and funnel math that produces repeatable closings, and choose the intermediary lane whose deal size, buyer pool, and fee structure match the companies you can actually source.
instructions: Work through the fields in order, because the seat economics and owner interview decide whether the remaining call, funnel, and outreach math is worth building at all.
Use real numbers from the offer you are evaluating, not hoped-for numbers, and write each dollar figure after clawbacks and splits are applied.
Interview the offer owner back before accepting the seat, and record every answer you received along with any question they dodged.
Check your funnel and close-rate figures weekly, not monthly, and diagnose any drop by identifying exactly which rate fell.
Finish by choosing one intermediary lane and confirming that your fee schedule and valuation rules match that lane's buyer pool.

fields.name: offer_commission_math
fields.prompt: Record the exact ticket price of the offer you plan to close, the commission percentage you will earn as setter, closer, self-setter, or affiliate, and the dollar amount that lands in your pocket per closed deal after any clawback risk.
fields.example: A $10K coaching offer paying the standard split: 10% closer, 5% setter, 15% self-set [Hudson Cosper — 4HgyBCSnkLE @ 00:07:25]. As a self-setter I earn $1,500 per deal, but refunds trigger clawbacks on commission already paid. Compare affiliates at 30 to 45 percent, where 45 percent of 20K is $9,000 [Asher Shaw — aFs-x6HJabU @ 00:05:58].

fields.name: owner_interview_questions
fields.prompt: List the questions you will ask the offer owner before accepting the seat, covering rep headcount, what current reps actually earn, how long the program has run, and which case studies and testimonials you will demand to see in writing.
fields.example: I asked: How many reps are on the team? What do reps make? How long has this program run? Send me case studies and testimonials [Colby Lyman — IlInXj9aPFg @ 00:03:13]. I also asked for proof of the call numbers, since under 20 calls a week is a flag [Frankie Isaac — _ZU2OAxnSMI @ 00:08:56].

fields.name: red_flag_screen
fields.prompt: Screen the seat against the disqualifiers: pay-to-apply terms, murky commission language, tickets under 2K, guaranteed-income pitches, and thin calendars. Write each flag you found, the evidence behind it, and whether it kills the seat outright or simply needs clarification.
fields.example: Seat A asked for a $297 application fee and promised '10K guaranteed', so it is dead on two counts [Hudson Cosper — 4HgyBCSnkLE @ 00:08:04]. Seat B sells a $1,500 ticket, under the 2K floor. Seat C pays 10% in writing but books only 12 calls a week, under 20 [Frankie Isaac — _ZU2OAxnSMI @ 00:08:56].

fields.name: daily_call_and_close_targets
fields.prompt: Set your daily call volume, typical call length, and minimum acceptable close rate. Then state the target close rate you are working toward and the specific number of calls per week you need to hit your monthly commission goal.
fields.example: I will take 6 calls a day, each a 30-45 minute diagnostic call. My floor is a 30-40% close rate, and my target is the 70-80% Cosper sets for closers on 5-10 calls a day [Hudson Cosper — 4HgyBCSnkLE @ 00:15:12]. At 30 calls a week and 35%, that is about 10 closes weekly.

fields.name: funnel_reverse_math
fields.prompt: Reverse-engineer your weekly funnel from one buyer backward. Write the visitor count, page-to-application rate, applications, bookings, calls held, and close rate you are assuming, and flag which stage you will check first when weekly results drop. Note why that stage matters most.
fields.example: Using ZK's math: about 170 visitors, 8-9 applications at 20-25%, 5 bookings, 3-4 calls held, and 1 buyer at roughly one in three [Scale Like ZK — uBQvqV_-nz0 @ 00:01:09]. I check KPIs weekly and look at show rate first, because a bad show rate alone can turn $50K into $5K [Scale Like ZK — uBQvqV_-nz0 @ 00:13:44].

fields.name: cash_on_hand_qualifier
fields.prompt: Write the exact cash-on-hand question you will place on the application, the dollar threshold that triggers a cancelled call, and the low-ticket downsell you will offer instead so that unqualified prospects never burn a closer slot. Include where the book-a-call invite sits.
fields.example: Application question: How much cash do you have on hand to invest right now? A '$500' answer means I cancel or offer the low-ticket downsell rather than burn a closer slot [Scale Like ZK — uBQvqV_-nz0 @ 00:07:41]. The book-a-call invite sits on the thank-you page, where the most excitement happens [Hernan Vazquez — PeOr6rOEN2Q @ 00:04:04].

fields.name: discovery_and_objection_script
fields.prompt: Draft your pain-first discovery opening and the what, why, and how probes you will use when an objection appears. Explain how your process is designed so that objections rarely surface, and what you do when one still does.
fields.example: I open on pain before any pitch. If the prospect says 'I need to think about it,' I act really dumb: What specifically? Why now? How would you decide? Every objection is a smokescreen [Daniel Coutts — RHobLxb_gLQ @ 00:15:24]. The goal is no objections if discovery is done correctly [Daniel Coutts — RHobLxb_gLQ @ 00:12:32].

fields.name: seat_outreach_plan
fields.prompt: Plan how you will land the seat itself as a sales process. Record your daily DM count, Loom length, target number of Looms before you review results, and the interview conversion you expect based on documented student outcomes.
fields.example: I send 100 DMs a day to offer owners and attach a 60-second Loom to every warm reply. I will review results after 30 Looms, because Isaac's student Lucas landed nine interviews from 30, and another student, Adam, earned $9K in month one [Frankie Isaac — _ZU2OAxnSMI @ 00:25:32]. My benchmark: roughly 3 interviews per 10 Looms.

fields.name: intermediary_lane_choice
fields.prompt: Choose your lane on the intermediary ladder: Main Street business broker, M&A advisor, or investment banker. Record the deal size band, typical buyer pool, fee structure, and why the companies you can source actually fit that lane rather than the next one up.
fields.example: Main Street broker: owner-operated companies under $1 million in SDE, sold to individual buyers through web listings at a 10% to 15% success fee with nothing upfront. My clients run $400K SDE, under the $3 million to $5 million EBITDA band where most PE groups show interest [Exit On Your Terms — Dx_mEuS7ipk @ 00:03:26], so auctions alone fail.

fields.name: fee_and_valuation_discipline
fields.prompt: Write your fee schedule and the valuation rules you refuse to break. Include any double Lehman math, upfront fee terms and what they are tied to, and the documents you must review before quoting any price to a seller.
fields.example: On a $4M sale, double Lehman pays 10% of the first million, then 8%, 6%, and 4%: $280,000 [CompassPointCapital — bjJIoxsFNY8 @ 00:01:33]. Any upfront fee is tied to a deliverable such as an accredited appraiser's valuation [CompassPointCapital — bjJIoxsFNY8 @ 00:00:37]. I never quote a price before seeing the returns [Ryan C. Winter, Business Broker — If4qHRijbWg @ 00:01:59].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not accept the seat or sign a mandate until every field is complete, the owner interview has produced written proof of rep earnings and call volume, no disqualifying red flag remains open, your weekly funnel math reaches at least one buyer, and your chosen lane matches the buyer pool your sourced companies can reach.

worksheets.title: Broker-Dealer Exposure, Licensing, and Supervision Controls
worksheets.purpose: Determine whether a deal places you inside broker-dealer law, qualify it under the M&A broker exemption where possible, map every state with jurisdiction, and set the licensing, supervision, recordkeeping, and reserve controls that keep your fees collectible.
instructions: Start with the deal structure, because whether securities change hands decides which of the remaining fields carry real legal weight.
Treat every state where a buyer, seller, or business sits as a possible regulator, and fill the jurisdiction map before signing any engagement letter.
Write the reasonable belief on buyer control into the engagement letter first, then repeat it in the closing documents.
Route every dollar through a third-party escrow and record the escrow details here so no one on the team takes custody of funds.
Review the licensing, supervision, and recordkeeping fields whenever ownership changes, a new office opens, or a listing lands in a new state.

fields.name: securities_exposure_check
fields.prompt: Describe the deal structure and decide whether securities change hands. Note whether it is an asset sale, equity sale, F-reorg, equity exchange, or earnout, and record which elements would put you inside broker-dealer law whether you register or not.
fields.example: Seller wants a stock sale with an F-reorg, which is almost certainly a securities transaction. I am proposing a non-assignable earnout, which is usually not a security [International Business Brokers Association — 7mV4t9a4PvE @ 00:40:53]. Because equity may still change hands, I am treating this mandate as inside broker-dealer law and qualifying it under the M&A exemption.

fields.name: target_eligibility
fields.prompt: Confirm the target qualifies for the M&A broker exemption. Record whether it is privately held, not a public or shell company, has made no public offering, and, if Florida applies, whether it sits under the size cap. Cite the evidence you reviewed.
fields.example: Target is a privately held distributor with no Exchange Act registration or reports, no public offering, and no shell history [ALC Lawcast: Finance in Focus — bfazVN-7QhQ @ 00:03:17]. The seller is in Florida; cap check: prior fiscal year EBITDA of $3.1M, under $25M, and revenue under $250M [ALC Lawcast: Finance in Focus — rl3PWicoIaE @ 00:02:43].

fields.name: buyer_control_belief
fields.prompt: Document your reasonable belief that the buyer will take control and actively operate the business. State the ownership percentage acquired, the presumption threshold that applies federally or in Florida, and where this belief is written into your paperwork.
fields.example: Buyer acquires 60% of the equity, above both the 25% federal presumption and the 20% Florida presumption [ALC Lawcast: Finance in Focus — o-XOblDUBuI @ 00:02:38]. The reasonable belief on control and operation is written into the engagement letter and repeated in the closing documents [International Business Brokers Association — 7mV4t9a4PvE @ 00:21:04]. No buyer groups are involved.

fields.name: funds_and_escrow
fields.prompt: Explain how every dollar in this deal will move from buyer to seller without you taking custody. Name the third-party escrow, list what triggers release, and note any wire limits or verification steps that could delay closing day.
fields.example: All deposits and the purchase price go through a third-party escrow agent; I never touch funds in a securities deal [International Business Brokers Association — 7mV4t9a4PvE @ 00:21:44]. Release triggers on signed closing documents. My fee is protected only because I qualify; unregistered fees, even recouped expenses, become uncollectible [International Business Brokers Association — 7mV4t9a4PvE @ 00:11:48].

fields.name: state_jurisdiction_map
fields.prompt: Map every state where the buyer, seller, or business is located. For each state, record whether M&A broker relief exists, whether a real estate license or permit is required, and how you will cover any gap before signing the engagement letter.
fields.example: Seller and business are in Nevada; buyer is in Texas. Each state may have jurisdiction [International Business Brokers Association — 7mV4t9a4PvE @ 00:33:49]. Nevada requires a business broker permit on top of the real estate license [Business Broker Crowd Call — Wj1uuYyuyQk @ 00:02:38]. Texas is non-licensed. Coverage: 24 states have M&A relief; 26 plus DC do not.

fields.name: license_state_check
fields.prompt: Check the business location against the license-state list. Record whether the state requires a real estate license, a business broker permit, or securities registration, and what penalty you would face for selling there without the right credential.
fields.example: Business is in Florida, one of the 17 license states, where Law 475 requires a valid real estate license [We Sell Construction Businesses — JkYDV-Gr_qE @ 00:00:06]. Without it, I face disgorged fees, rescinded deals, and unpaid commissions; one unlicensed broker literally did not get paid [Business Broker Crowd Call — 22hjuZT2usA @ 00:03:33].

fields.name: non_license_state_boundaries
fields.prompt: If the deal sits in a non-license state, write the exact boundaries you will hold: where your work stops, who handles the lease assignment and any real estate, and which home-state standard you will act under for protection.
fields.example: Texas deal: I sell personal property freely but stop at the non-binding LOI and stay out of the lease assignment [Business Broker Crowd Call — Py7d57O-Rxs @ 00:02:21]. A licensed agent handles the real estate. I leave purchase agreement blanks alone, and I act under my home-state license rules [Business Broker Crowd Call — _4qKlVp4-8s @ 00:02:06].

fields.name: partner_licensee_plan
fields.prompt: When a listing lands in a licensed state where you hold nothing, name the local licensee you will partner with, whose name and license number go on the paperwork, how fees split, and what insurance covers the business sale.
fields.example: Florida listing, no Florida license: I partner with a local licensee whose name and license number go on all paperwork while I work in the background [Business Broker Crowd Call — Wj1uuYyuyQk @ 00:01:41]. Because eXp Realty E&O does not cover business sales, the partner sits at eXp Commercial with the business broker addendum.

fields.name: supervision_structure
fields.prompt: If you run or join a registered firm, describe the supervision structure. Record who approves new accounts, whether any office must operate as an OSJ, its inspection cycle, and which ownership changes would trigger a continuing membership application.
fields.example: New-account approval stays with the principal, so our branch manager does not create an OSJ with mandatory annual inspections; branches run on three-year cycles [The Finance Lab — dKOzaPUjfHM @ 00:07:12]. A 30% stake sale crosses the Rule 1017 trigger of 25%, so we file at least 30 days before the change [The Finance Lab — dKOzaPUjfHM @ 00:09:44].

fields.name: records_and_reserves
fields.prompt: Set your recordkeeping and reserve controls. Record your retention buckets, which records stay easily accessible, how fast you can produce records on a regulator's written demand, and how often you reconcile cash suspense and compute reserves for customer credits.
fields.example: Records sit in six-year and three-year buckets, with the latest two years easily accessible, because once the SEC drops a written demand we have exactly 14 days to produce [CertFuel — MhYKFYS6gTI @ 00:04:25]. Cash suspense is reconciled daily and large credit balances go up the line before they are resolved [FINOP Controller — -3SAUcV8ljM @ 00:09:03].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not sign the mandate or market the business until the target is confirmed private and non-shell, the buyer control belief is written into the engagement letter, every state with jurisdiction is mapped and covered by relief, a license, or a licensed partner, and all deal money is routed through a named third-party escrow.

worksheets.title: Non-Circumvention Protection and Yacht and Aircraft Entry Economics
worksheets.purpose: Choose and verify the right protective instrument before any disclosure, screen counterparties and clauses for fakes and buried terms, then build an entry plan, commission model, pricing discipline, and closing safeguards for a yacht or aircraft brokerage seat.
instructions: Complete the instrument, counterparty, and authenticity fields before sharing any protected name, price, or shipping detail with anyone.
Reject any document citing ICC 400, 500, or 600 regulations, or calling itself an ICC IMFPA, before reading further.
Read every draft line by line for buried non-competes and commission-liability language, and record what you struck.
Run the commission math on a realistic target sale using the tiered schedule, the co-broker split, and your house split.
Confirm every seat and closing safeguard in writing before you accept a brokerage seat or take on an acquisition mandate.

fields.name: nda_vs_ncnda
fields.prompt: Decide which instrument this disclosure needs: a plain NDA that only stops talking, or a non-circumvention agreement that stops the deal closing without you. Explain the specific risk that drove your choice and what each paper leaves uncovered.
fields.example: I am introducing a grain supplier to an importer, where nothing gets signed and the broker gets cut out [IXH TRADING Academy — 5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:07:09]. An NDA only stops talking; I need a clause stopping the deal closing without me [Attorney Nancy Greene — FOUV15TeRLY @ 00:01:00]. So I require a true NCNDA covering affiliates, survival period, and remedy.

fields.name: counterparty_identification
fields.prompt: Identify every counterparty before any disclosure. Record the authorized signatories, their government photo ID or KYC status, the client information sheet, registration and bank references, and how many intermediaries stand between you and the principal on both the buy and sell sides.
fields.example: Seller signatory verified by government photo ID and a completed client information sheet; no protected names, prices, or shipping data go out until execution [Trade Base Hub — yrJW_zsMUXM @ 00:00:33]. Registration and bank references checked first [IXH TRADING Academy — 5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:08:10]. Buy side shows two mandates before the principal, which is my limit.

fields.name: icc_authenticity
fields.prompt: Verify the paperwork is genuine before signing. Record the publication number cited, whether it quotes ICC 400, 500, or 600 regulations, whether it calls itself an IMFPA, and whether any advance fee is requested to issue documents or guarantees.
fields.example: The counterparty sent an 'ICC IMFPA' citing ICC 500 regulations. There is no such thing as an ICC IMFPA, so it went in the garbage bin [Cangem Global Corporation — HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:01:10]. I replaced it with ICC publication 769E, the 27-page model occasional intermediary contract bought from the ICC website and reusable for any number of deals.

fields.name: defined_opportunity_and_term
fields.prompt: Define the specific opportunity the agreement protects and the substantive non-public information being shared. Set the term in years, explain why it is reasonable for this sector, and confirm the document is executed before any disclosure happens.
fields.example: Opportunity: one named supplier's grain contract with one importer, plus supplier pricing and shipping schedules. Term is two years, the safe default within 2 to 5 years [IXH TRADING Academy — 5VMFuBur4kI @ 00:02:58]. Even 3 years will be a hard bet, and beyond that is daydreaming [Cangem Global Corporation — HldBP9R47Bg @ 00:09:43]. Signed before disclosure.

fields.name: clause_review
fields.prompt: Read the draft line by line for buried terms. Record any non-compete, non-solicitation, or commission-liability language, how broadly the restricted work is defined, what you crossed out, and which governing law and dispute forum you selected and why.
fields.example: As buyer, I crossed out language making me liable for the broker's commission, since that sits between seller and broker [David C Barnett Small Business and Deal Making SMB — wHxYmcrcq4M @ 00:07:36]. I also struck a two-year non-compete defined as broadly as video production [Rafael Ludwig — WjchmVIKv5M @ 00:02:08]. Governing law left blank; ICC arbitration chosen.

fields.name: execution_and_remedy
fields.prompt: Record how the agreement will be executed and enforced. Note the e-signature platform, whether signing unlocks a data room, the liquidated damages clause, the arbitration seat, and whether your client is likely to be plaintiff or defendant.
fields.example: Confidentiality agreement goes out by DocuSign and auto-grants data-room access on signing, as roughly 99% of CRE agreements now do [Adventures in CRE — EL2eIKZ_OV8 @ 00:01:01]. A liquidated damages clause sets the remedy. My seller client would be the plaintiff in any breach, so I chose arbitration, the plaintiff-friendly forum [Adventures in CRE — EL2eIKZ_OV8 @ 00:03:33].

fields.name: yacht_aircraft_entry_plan
fields.prompt: Lay out your entry plan into yacht or aircraft brokerage. Record the hub you will live in, the first yachting or aviation job you will take, whether your state licenses brokers, and the captains or managers you will farm for leads.
fields.example: I am moving to a Florida yacht hub, because to succeed you need to live where there are yachts and yacht owners [Yacht Broker Masterclass — -7bW4uN98Hc @ 00:00:00]. Florida is one of two states licensing yacht brokers, so I will get licensed. I will take any yachting job first and farm captains and managers weekly for leads.

fields.name: commission_schedule_math
fields.prompt: Work the commission math for a realistic target sale. Apply the tiered yacht schedule or aircraft percentage, the co-broker split between buyer and seller sides, and your house split, then write the net dollars that actually reach you.
fields.example: A $30M yacht carries $1.75M: 10% on the first $10M, 5% on the next $10M, 2.5% on the last $10M [Yachts For Sale — FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:05:18]. Representing the buyer, I take 60%, or $1.05M [Yacht Broker Masterclass — _Shd1I2mefI @ 00:06:24]. On a 50/50 house split I keep $525,000.

fields.name: pricing_and_listing_discipline
fields.prompt: Write the asking price strategy you will present to the owner. Record the number you will ask, where you expect it to land, the fantasy number you refuse to promise, and how you will move on off-market aircraft offers.
fields.example: I advised asking 30 to land near 27 rather than win the listing on 35 and watch it sit two years [Yachts For Sale — FpmvbD9-7yc @ 00:25:05]. On off-market aircraft I move early and treat the first offer as one of the best before it becomes a stinky fish [Own The Jet — i36Xg_tsVAY @ 00:15:19].

fields.name: seat_and_closing_safeguards
fields.prompt: Before accepting a brokerage seat or acquisition mandate, record whether base pay is a clawback advance, the escrow arrangement for closing, the team you will assemble up front, and any deposit or retainer you will collect on the buy side.
fields.example: Confirmed in writing: my base pay is a clawback advance recovered from my first sale [Yacht Broker Masterclass — _Shd1I2mefI @ 00:03:06]. Every closing runs through escrow [Alex Bengoechea — p6XXGAWrnB8 @ 00:21:23]. Jet acquisitions: aviation tax adviser, finance, escrow agent, escrow agreement, and broker contract up front, plus a retainer [Own The Jet — i36Xg_tsVAY @ 00:18:24].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not disclose protected information, accept a brokerage seat, or open a listing until a verified non-circumvention instrument with identified signatories is executed, every fake ICC reference is rejected, buried clauses are struck, your net commission is calculated after all splits, and base pay, escrow, and retainer terms are confirmed in writing.

worksheets.title: Commission Lock and Brokerage Build Plan
worksheets.purpose: Secure every fee in writing before a single identifier leaves your hands, harden closing-day wires against loss, and design a brokerage pricing, recruiting, and overhead model that survives thin margins, agent attrition, and long sale cycles.
instructions: Complete every field with figures from a live or recently closed deal, not a hypothetical one.
Release no tail numbers, serial numbers, or maintenance reports until the fee-lock fields are signed and filed.
Treat closing-day wires as the main point of loss and confirm every bank contact by an independent call.
Price your brokerage on value and ancillary revenue, never on the cheapest split alone.
Revisit the recruiting, overhead, and seller-deposit fields every quarter as agent count and deal volume change.

fields.name: written_fee_lock
fields.prompt: Before any aircraft, yacht, or business package leaves your hands, write the exact document that locks your fee. Name the instrument, the principal it binds, the percentage or flat figure, and the moment payment triggers at closing, so nobody can argue later.
fields.example: One-page commission agreement naming the buyer, because 'the most important thing is that you have something in writing that says how you're going to get paid before you start sending specs' [The Ultimate Jet Guide — 1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:05:44]. On a 2006 Hawker 850 XB sold for $5M, 1.5% equals $75,000 [Alex Bengoechea — Uhqo4raDQ0k @ 00:00:38].

fields.name: scrubbed_spec_sheet
fields.prompt: List every identifier you will strip from the first package until a signed fee agreement exists. Cover tail numbers, serial numbers, maintenance reports, and cockpit photos, and state who checks each image before anything is sent to a co-broker.
fields.example: Scrubbed spec sheet only: no tail number, no serial number, no maintenance reports [The Ultimate Jet Guide — 1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:05:44]. Second reviewer zooms into every cockpit photo, because a visible tail number there is where packages leak most often [The Ultimate Jet Guide — 1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:01:38]. Full logs release only after the commission agreement is countersigned and filed.

fields.name: co_broker_fee_figure
fields.prompt: Write the exact dollar figure you will counter with when a co-broker offers 'whatever you think.' Separate an introduction-only fee from a closing-work fee, and note what happens to your fee if a pre-buy squawk cuts the price by a hundred grand.
fields.example: Intro only: $10,000. Intro plus closing work: $25,000 [The Ultimate Jet Guide — 1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:08:01]. Fixed figure, not a spread, because 'if it goes into pre-buy, then there's squawks and they have to reduce the price by a hundred grand, and now you get paid nothing' [The Ultimate Jet Guide — 1ILeO7AapJM @ 00:04:39].

fields.name: chain_length_check
fields.prompt: Map every entity standing between you and the actual principal on this deal. Count the intermediaries, name each one, and decide in writing whether the chain passes your walk-away rule before you invest another hour chasing the fee.
fields.example: Chain: me, a mandate holder, a second broker, then the principal's office. That is two entities between me and the principal, the upper limit. An NCNDA that arrived listing 14 intermediaries was declined the same day, per the walk-away rule [Sam Cutting - Red Flags Verification — QguZjBADFoA @ 00:00:42]. Principal contact verified by direct call before signing.

fields.name: wire_verification_protocol
fields.prompt: Describe the exact wire-verification sequence for closing day. Specify the test-wire amount, how you will confirm it, where the phone number comes from, and what you will do within the first 72 hours if funds are misdirected, and who owns each step.
fields.example: Send a small test wire first, confirm receipt through a number looked up independently or in person at the office, never one taken from the email [Family Split Strategy — DZe5D7_TCDA @ 00:09:23]. If funds are misdirected, file with IC3 and call contacts at both banks, since reversal usually happens within 72 hours [Family Split Strategy — DZe5D7_TCDA @ 00:10:24].

fields.name: disbursement_form_check
fields.prompt: Audit the disbursement form two days before closing. List every agent-side field, the funding entity's wire amount, bank name, and contact details, and record who confirmed each item and when the funding entity was last contacted. Note any daily wire limit.
fields.example: Title attorney coached to list the wire amount, their bank's name, and their contact information so a failed transfer can be traced [Equity Real Estate — mVFdzEqW2M4 @ 00:00:51]. Funding entity called 48 hours ahead; every field checked, because a clean form pays by direct deposit within 24 hours [Equity Real Estate — mVFdzEqW2M4 @ 00:01:21]. Buyer's daily wire cap confirmed.

fields.name: brokerage_pricing_model
fields.prompt: Choose the split and fee structure your brokerage will charge agents. State the split, any cap, transaction fee, and servicing fee, then estimate your margin and explain how the model survives without relying on a flat fee alone.
fields.example: Start at 70/30 with a $500 transaction fee and a 2.25% servicing fee, the structure Garth Ward rebuilt toward after a 90/10 split with a $15K cap, while still running near 10% margins at multi-office scale [Mike Sherrard — OFzI2gK-nps @ 00:33:14]. No $500 flat-fee-only model, which Joe Mendoza calls a path to going broke without ancillary revenue.

fields.name: recruiting_target_profile
fields.prompt: Define the agent you will recruit first. Give the production band, the custom presentation you will build for each appointment, the retention evidence that justifies skipping new-licensee seminars in favor of experienced producers, and the day-one event that seeds your roster.
fields.example: Target $2-10M producers, the pivot Jim Remley made after 87% attrition from new-agent seminars [Smart Agents — YKfvldXPHWw @ 00:08:38]. Each appointment gets a custom deck, treated like a million-dollar listing [Mike Sherrard — OFzI2gK-nps @ 00:14:03]. Seed event: a coffee-shop gathering, the format where Garth Ward signed 10+ agents on day one.

fields.name: overhead_and_management
fields.prompt: Set your overhead triggers. State the agent count at which you will sign a long office lease, when a manager joins, and how every advertisement, including social media posts, will display your broker ID and license number.
fields.example: No long lease before 30 to 40 agents, following Ward's 80 sq ft broom-closet first office [Mike Sherrard — OFzI2gK-nps @ 00:10:07]. Manager hired early, since re-routing agents later hurt culture [Mike Sherrard — OFzI2gK-nps @ 00:29:15]. Broker ID and license number on every ad, no blind ads [Dee Kumar Real Estate — V5gUCAcegsY @ 00:04:15].

fields.name: seller_deposit_terms
fields.prompt: Write the commitment terms you will require from a business seller before working the deal. Include the deposit amount, how it credits toward the success fee, any performance guarantee, and the follow-up cadence you will run with each serious buyer.
fields.example: $15K to $20K seller deposit credited toward the success fee [Business Broker Growth — 7jkOz9WXEh8 @ 00:43:36]. Refunded if no solid LOI from a qualified buyer with access to capital arrives within 90 days [Business Broker Growth — 7jkOz9WXEh8 @ 00:09:54]. Fifteen-touch follow-up cadence; five deals carried at once on a seven-month average sale cycle.

worksheets.completion_gate: Signed commission agreement on file, scrubbed spec sheet approved, intermediary chain at two entities or fewer, test-wire protocol rehearsed, disbursement form complete two days before closing, and brokerage split, lease trigger, recruiting profile, and seller deposit terms written down.

worksheets.title: Off-Market Pipeline and Valuation Worksheet
worksheets.purpose: Build a disciplined off-market outreach engine that reaches owners who already lean toward selling, qualify them by phone before any meeting, then price each business on normalized earnings, a defensible multiple, lender-ready coverage, and a closable structure.
instructions: Build the list and sending infrastructure before writing a single line of outreach copy.
Never ask an owner outright whether they want to sell; lead with a guide, prospectus, or valuation.
Book no meeting until a caller has confirmed trailing-twelve-month revenue and EBITDA.
Start every valuation from the tax return, since lenders treat returns as the source of truth.
Run coverage and structure math before listing, not after a buyer's lender pushes back.

fields.name: target_list_build
fields.prompt: Define the owner list you will build for off-market outreach. Name the data source, the headcount filter, the scraping method and cost per search, and how you will re-import the company list before any sequence starts sending.
fields.example: Apollo search filtered by employee headcount in one service niche, scraped through Export List at about $50 per search URL, then the company list is re-imported into Apollo [Nick Abraham — Wdk1N79_WyM @ 00:04:22]. The benchmark is Equity Front Capital's campaign, which produced 142 meeting-ready leads [Nick Abraham — Wdk1N79_WyM @ 00:00:43].

fields.name: sending_infrastructure
fields.prompt: Describe your sending infrastructure. List the secondary domains and inboxes, the platform you send from, the spare capacity you will hold, and the bounce-rate signal that forces you to rotate a mailbox out of the active pool.
fields.example: Secondary inboxes only, sent through Smartlead, because 'never send from your primary domain, because it ruins your deliverability' [Nick Abraham — Wdk1N79_WyM @ 00:05:04]. Hold about 50 percent spare inbox capacity and rotate out any mailbox throwing high bounce rates [Wolf of Main Street — FZ98S2zrji0 @ 00:12:27]. No .edu or institutional domains.

fields.name: cold_email_copy
fields.prompt: Draft the first cold email exactly as it will be sent. Keep it plain text, count the words, and state the single yes-or-no question you end on, plus the guide, prospectus, or valuation you are offering instead of asking to buy.
fields.example: Plain text, 48 words, no links, no images, no name or firm in the copy, ending with one question: would a short guide on what businesses like yours sell for be useful? [Wolf of Main Street — FZ98S2zrji0 @ 00:04:05]. Valuation offer saved for the follow-up, the opener Nick Abraham favors, never 'are you looking to sell' [Paul Macaluso — Cn4V6pWhbMk @ 00:02:44].

fields.name: seven_touch_sequence
fields.prompt: Lay out your full multi-channel touch sequence by day. Specify each email, call, social, and handwritten-letter touch, how each references the one before, and what personal detail, such as the receptionist's name, you will reuse on later touches.
fields.example: Seven touches: day 1 email, day 3 call, day 5 social, day 8 email, day 12 handwritten letter, day 15 call, day 20 email. Every touch references the previous one, and later touches use the receptionist's name [Wolf of Main Street — FZ98S2zrji0 @ 00:03:35]. Cold owners stay on a long-term nurture, so 'no' becomes 'not yet' [Paul Macaluso — Cn4V6pWhbMk @ 00:00:35].

fields.name: phone_qualification_gate
fields.prompt: Write the qualification script your caller runs before any calendar invite goes out. List the trailing-twelve-month revenue and EBITDA questions, the minimum size you accept, and the Do Not Call check completed on every number before dialing or texting.
fields.example: Caller asks for trailing-12-month revenue and EBITDA before booking, because 'a lot of the people replying are very small businesses' [Nick Abraham — Wdk1N79_WyM @ 00:07:45]. Every number is checked against the Do Not Call list first, with no spam texts [Brandon Thomas — vOB7Te243ew @ 00:03:52]. Expect one live owner per five dials, as LoCasa reached about 5 of 28.

fields.name: pipeline_stage_definitions
fields.prompt: Define every stage in your CRM pipeline from first touch to signed engagement. For each stage, state the entry criterion, the required document, the follow-up flag in days, and the diligence items that must exist before a deal advances.
fields.example: Stages in HubSpot: Contacted, Qualified by phone, Confidentiality Signed, Financials Received, Diligence. A 5-day follow-up flag sits on every open record [Smart Agents — YKfvldXPHWw @ 00:27:56]. No deal moves past Diligence without 3 years of tax returns, a customer-concentration check, and a quality-of-earnings review of about $15K [Frankie Finance — 1PRKZu79Zg4 @ 00:16:31].

fields.name: earnings_basis_and_sde
fields.prompt: Rebuild the target's normalized earnings from the tax return outward. Choose SDE or adjusted EBITDA based on size, list net profit, owner salary, and each add-back line, and total the figure a buyer will actually pay a multiple on.
fields.example: Under roughly $500K-$1M of earnings, so SDE applies. Peter Nola's bakery math: $100K of profit plus a $50K owner salary plus a $10K car equals $160K of SDE [Peter Nola — RoGz5NZF96I @ 00:01:16]. PPP money and a lawsuit settlement removed as non-operating income; recruiter fees added back as one-time [Nate Lind - Business Broker and Beyond — yaZZzBKh86I @ 00:01:39].

fields.name: multiple_selection
fields.prompt: Select the multiple you will defend and justify it. Name the size band, the comparable range, and how owner dependence, customer concentration, trend, recurring revenue, and clean books push the number up or down from the midpoint.
fields.example: Owner-operated, $160K SDE, so the working range is 2-3.5x SDE [Deal Street - Small to Lower Middle Market M&A — ggUaT-lHV0A @ 00:04:13]. Clean books and a rising trend support 3x; heavy owner dependence keeps it below 3.5x. Never listed on revenue, because 'buyers buy cash flow, not revenue' [Deal Street - Small to Lower Middle Market M&A — ggUaT-lHV0A @ 00:01:08].

fields.name: dscr_and_lender_fit
fields.prompt: Run debt service coverage before listing. State the SBA floor, the lender appetite you are testing against, the buyer injection, how you treat the buyer's livable wage, and which lender matches your add-back schedule on salary and depreciation.
fields.example: DSCR run at 1.5, above the 1.25 SBA floor, and again with a 20 percent down-payment return [Brent Freeman  - The CBB Group — pzqh4R8Hppk @ 00:12:28]. Tax returns treated as the source of truth. Lender chosen because it adds back owner salary in full, since lenders vary on salary and depreciation [Keira Hamilton — 1dJeO4qEAhU @ 00:02:40].

fields.name: deal_structure_stack
fields.prompt: Design the deal structure that bridges headline price and cash at closing. Specify the SBA debt, buyer injection, seller note amortization and balloon, any earnout, and how a rollover or equity exchange changes the securities analysis.
fields.example: 10% buyer injection, SBA 7(a) debt for the balance, plus a seller note amortized over 10-plus years with a balloon at year 3 to 5 that usually gets refinanced [Deal Street - Small to Lower Middle Market M&A — a5Z--B3Uhrg @ 00:05:13]. Any earnout kept non-assignable; equity exchanges treated as securities transactions [International Business Brokers Association — 7mV4t9a4PvE @ 00:40:53].

worksheets.completion_gate: Owner list scraped and re-imported, secondary inboxes warmed with spare capacity, sub-60-word email approved, seven-touch sequence scheduled, phone qualification script in use, pipeline stages defined, normalized earnings tied to returns, multiple justified, DSCR passing at 1.5, and deal structure drafted.

worksheets.title: Specialist Markets and Closing Certainty Worksheet
worksheets.purpose: Price digital businesses, tower leases, powered land, and transferred tax credits on the paper rather than the pitch, then carry any deal from honest presentation through binding exclusivity, protected post-closing claims, and a controlled timeline to funded close.
instructions: Benchmark every specialist offer against a published fee ladder or multiple before discussing price.
Demand actual figures over annualized ones and signed agreements over promised ones.
Disclose known problems before listing, because a problem found at week six lands as broken trust.
Judge competing offers on certainty of close after price, not on headline number alone.
Keep part of the seller's money in your pocket and keep every milestone moving inside the month.

fields.name: digital_broker_selection
fields.prompt: Compare the brokers or marketplaces you would use to sell or buy a digital business. Record each one's commission ladder, minimum fee, buyer fee, close rate, and how tightly it controls confidential details in the teaser.
fields.example: Quiet Light: 10% of the first $1M plus 9% on the next $500,000, so $145,000 on a $1.5M sale [Colin Matcha — l-9E6P1CSEc @ 00:08:09]. Empire Flippers: $7,000 minimum, then 15% up to about $700,000 [Business Solution — zcYOmZ8cAGE @ 00:01:36]. FE International: 94% of listings closed, buyer fee of $1,000 or less.

fields.name: digital_underwriting_window
fields.prompt: Set the minimum data window you will underwrite for an online business. State how many months of actual revenue and profit you require, which traffic pulls you request, and which code-level red flags you search for first.
fields.example: Listing annualized on the last three months was rejected; six months of actual figures plus targeted traffic pulls requested [Colin Matcha — r4fmjknWB7o @ 00:06:30]. SaaS code reviewed for lifetime plans, discounting, and founder dependence before diligence opens, since 'lifetime plans are suicidal for a SaaS valuation' and one surfaced within 24 hours [Quiet Light Brokerage — oJsHo5vaDus @ 00:39:54].

fields.name: saas_off_market_sourcing
fields.prompt: Describe how you will find SaaS or website deals before they reach a public listing. Name the communities you will join, the exact business type and budget you will announce, and the broker newsletters you will brief.
fields.example: Post in SaaS Facebook groups and forums that I am buying, because some owners who never considered selling say yes once asked [Jaryd Krause - Buying Online Businesses — XbluQ7u-9nc @ 00:03:20]. Brief FE International's newsletter team with the exact SaaS type and budget so only matching deals arrive [Jaryd Krause - Buying Online Businesses — XbluQ7u-9nc @ 00:01:23].

fields.name: tower_lease_benchmark
fields.prompt: Benchmark a cell tower lease buyout offer before anyone signs. Record annual rent, whether a right of first refusal exists, the resulting multiple, the easement versus lease structure, and how a lender objection on title would be handled.
fields.example: Annual rent $24,000 with a right of first refusal, so a fair offer lands near 16-17x, or $384,000 to $408,000 [Tower Genius — V2LGinURueI @ 00:01:03]. Perpetual easement weighed for a bigger upfront check [SiteBid Infrastructure — EsfznycDU6I @ 00:01:30]. If the lender objects, structure it as a Master Lease so no easement shows [Nexus Towers — YjzN5Uo5yf8 @ 00:01:35].

fields.name: powered_land_and_credits
fields.prompt: Before paying a powered-land premium or buying a transferred tax credit, list the documents you demand. Cover the power agreement, dated load ramp, off ramp, and how you will verify a credit beyond its IRS registration number.
fields.example: Powered land: signed power agreement, a dated load ramp, and an off ramp if power or a moratorium blocks the build [Reed Smith LLP — HXjpQWcZ6F8 @ 00:02:17]. Section 6418 credit: registration number is not proof of validity, because the buyer bears the IRS risk after transfer and must recover from the seller [Andrew Dubinsky — h0qEAIoQ4Jo @ 00:08:50].

fields.name: books_to_returns_tie_out
fields.prompt: Tie the seller's last three years of tax returns to the P&L line by line. List every mismatch, every add-back lacking a receipt, and every disclosure item such as settled suits, state tax matters, and change-of-control leases.
fields.example: Three years of returns tied to the P&L; two add-backs without receipts stripped before going to market [CHARLES WEATHERLY — 55kqfOfgIZw @ 00:01:47]. A settled suit and a change-of-control lease disclosed before listing, because a problem found at week six lands as broken trust [Charles Weatherly — 55kqfOfgIZw @ 00:05:09]. Matching returns made a $450,000 educational product SBA pre-qualified.

fields.name: cim_honesty_review
fields.prompt: Outline your confidential information memorandum and flag every weakness you will disclose openly. State how projections for new product lines are handled, who drafts each section, and how quickly you commit to answering buyer data requests once diligence begins.
fields.example: CIM discloses customer concentration and owner dependence up front, because 'hiding weaknesses only creates distrust' [iGOTHAM — r1DSXPxZzu8 @ 00:00:48]. New product line priced through structure, not hockey-stick projections [Amped Success - Matt Uhler — uG64e1KV1S0 @ 00:37:45]. Data requests answered inside the month, since stretching to three months turns buyers off [Amped Success - Matt Uhler — uG64e1KV1S0 @ 00:09:26].

fields.name: loi_terms_and_exclusivity
fields.prompt: Draft the key LOI terms you will accept or offer. Separate binding from non-binding provisions, state the exclusivity window, and explain how you will judge certainty of close rather than headline price when comparing competing offers.
fields.example: Binding exclusivity of 60 to 90 days; price and terms non-binding [My SBA Loan Pro Podcast — VaF6Cv0koYQ @ 00:11:21]. After price, the deciding criterion is certainty of close, 'because anyone can write a good offer' [Carter Morse & Goodrich — a71tQJb9UFE @ 00:00:02]. A 100% seller-financed 'full price' LOI was rejected, since the seller keeps the risk without the money.

fields.name: post_close_protection
fields.prompt: Choose how post-closing claims will be covered for this transaction. State whether you use escrow, a seller-note set-off, indemnity caps, or representation and warranty insurance, the percentage held, the hold period, and the deal size triggering each tool.
fields.example: Main Street deal of $1M: $800K SBA debt, $100K buyer cash, $100K subordinated seller note with set-off rights instead of escrow, which is market on Main Street [SMB Law Group LLP — LASFByP_8g4 @ 00:07:37]. On a $10M deal, a 10 to 20 percent indemnity cap holds $1M to $2M for 12 to 18 months [HALO Talks — 76I0zKp5FM0 @ 00:15:14].

fields.name: closing_timeline_control
fields.prompt: Build the closing calendar from signed LOI to funded close. Assign week-by-week milestones, the person owning each, the point where deal fatigue usually sets in, and the escalation you trigger when any milestone slips past its date.
fields.example: Target close inside 3 to 6 months, with fatigue expected at months 4 to 6 [Amped Success - Matt Uhler — uG64e1KV1S0 @ 00:16:06]. Weekly status call with lender, attorney, and escrow agent; any slip over five business days escalates to principals the same day, because 'simply put, time kills all deals' [M&A Synergy AI — h3OE0enrIxg @ 00:01:58].

worksheets.completion_gate: Broker fee ladders compared, six months of actual digital figures in hand, tower offer benchmarked at 16 to 18 times rent, power and credit documents verified, returns tied to the P&L with receipts, honest CIM approved, LOI exclusivity set, set-off or indemnity terms agreed, and closing calendar owned week by week.
